speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) what enforcement power is vested with the Government other than to name and make public the egregious businesses who raise prices unjustifiably using GST increase as a cover; and (b) what are the expectations on merchants in order to meet transparency on their pricing and in their communications with consumers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The CAP works with various partners to reach out to businesses to guard against GST profiteering.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Businesses are encouraged to be transparent in their communication on price adjustments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The Consumers Association of Singapore (CASE) publishes best practices on price display and communication.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Our trade association partners have also been guiding their members in clearly communicating any price adjustments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: For instance, the Federation of Merchants' Associations Singapore (FMAS) and the Heartland Enterprise Centre Singapore (HECS) have conducted extensive outreach and walkabouts in coffee shops, in Housing and Development Board (HDB) shops and hawker centres to remind their members of the need to be transparent about their pricing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Consumers can also report potential instances of GST misrepresentation to the CAP via three methods: the CAP's online feedback form, the hotline, or at any of our 112 Community Centres.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: This is to facilitate easy price comparisons and for them to avoid falling prey to unjustified price hikes.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We keep a very close watch on the prices of essential goods through the Consumer Price Index (CPI).

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We review and share the CPI survey regularly.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The CPI is compiled by DOS and measures the average price changes of a fixed basket of consumption goods and services commonly purchased by resident households over time.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: MTI and the Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore (CCCS) have been working very closely with CASE, in particular, since a few years ago and especially in the last one year, to further strengthen Price Kaki.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: At the touch of a button, you will be able to see the items within your vicinity and you have choices.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: This is really what we want: free market competition and for consumers and fellow Singaporeans to have a wide range of choices.
